arxiv-2207-13972.title: Photonic sampled and quantized analog-to- digital converters on thin-film lithium niobate platform Journal: osajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2207-13972.creator: Donghe Tu, \authormark 1,2 Xingrui Huang, \authormark 1,2 Yang Liu, \authormark 1,2 Zhiguo Yu, \authormark 1 and Zhiyong Li \authormark 1,*
arxiv-2207-13972.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Donghe Tu, \authormark 1,2 Xingrui Huang, \authormark 1,2 Yang Liu, \authormark 1,2 Zhiguo Yu, \authormark 1 and Zhiyong Li \authormark 1,*. In this paper, an on-chip photonic sampled and quantized analog-to-digital converter (ADC) on thin-film lithium niobate platform is experimentally demonstrated. Using two phase modulators as a sampler and a 5 × \times 5 multimode interference (MMI) coupler as a quantizer, an 1 GHz sinusoidal analog input signal was successfully converted to a digitized output with a 20 GSample/s sampling rate.

arxiv-2212-03892.title: Prethermal fragmentation in a periodically driven Fermionic chain
arxiv-2212-03892.creator: Somsubhra Ghosh 1 , Indranil Paul 2 , and K. Sengupta 1
arxiv-2212-03892.description: Abstract We study a Fermionic chain with nearest-neighbor hopping and density-density interactions, where the nearest-neighbor interaction term is driven periodically. We show that such a driven chain exhibits prethermal strong Hilbert space fragmentation (HSF) in the high drive amplitude regime at specific drive frequencies ω m ∗ \omega_{m}^{\ast} . This constitutes the first realization of HSF for out-of-equilibrium systems.

arxiv-2404-10118.title: Stochastic Thermodynamics at the Quantum-Classical Boundary: A Self-Consistent Framework Based on Adiabatic-Response Theory
arxiv-2404-10118.creator: Joshua Eglinton, Federico Carollo, Igor Lesanovsky, Kay Brandner
arxiv-2404-10118.description: Abstract Microscopic thermal machines promise to play an important role in future quantum technologies. Making such devices widely applicable will require effective strategies to channel their output into easily accessible storage systems like classical degrees of freedom. Here, we develop a self-consistent theoretical framework that makes it possible to model such quantum-classical hybrid devices in a thermodynamically consistent manner.

arxiv-2509-12031.title: Contractive kinetic Langevin samplers beyond global Lipschitz continuity
arxiv-2509-12031.creator: Iosif Lytras, Panayotis Mertikopoulos
arxiv-2509-12031.description: Abstract In this paper, we examine the problem of sampling from log-concave distributions with (possibly) superlinear gradient growth under kinetic (underdamped) Langevin algorithms. Using a carefully tailored taming scheme, we propose two novel discretizations of the kinetic Langevin SDE, and we show that they are both contractive and satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality.
